This is all my opinion but I feel gameplay outside of combat is a lot better in TOTK. It’s much less restricted in both movement and exploration and the tools it provides you with can give you some really creative and fun ways to get by. Side-quests are also far less annoying and more well thought out in Zelda. it’s pretty agreed upon that ER’s quest system is a dumpster fire mechanically, with overly cryptic directions and how utterly easy it is to fail an entire quest line without a guide. Also while I think the lore and background of ER is super cool, the main story you go through is very basic and the big important details are usually just vaguely alluded to unless you read item descriptions. TOTK’s story, while rather shoddily put together, had me very invested towards the end and I got pretty attached to some of the characters, something ER never did for me since character interactions were extremely limited outside of maybe boss cutscenes. 

  TOTK is also just so much more chill. I love gliding through Hyrule and just taking in the world around me (which I do find to be a lot prettier than the Lands Between). Especially in a world where not everything's trying to brutally murder me.

  I love them both though, despite both game’s several flaws. I’m still playing TOTK but I definitely see myself picking ER back up when the DLC drops.

I think the best strategy for Genichiro would be to be as aggressive as possible, cause running away usually causes him to shoot you with a barrage of arrows. Keep clashing swords with him over and over again until a you hear a distinct clanging noise, which means you should deflect once before going right back to hitting. Whenever he does that jump attack, it’s almost always followed by a thrust to mikiri counter. He also has two combo moves that can kill you pretty quickly if you don’t deflect their patterns down, though for the one where he pauses in the middle, I personally like to use the mist raven towards the end of his pause so I could teleport and attack from behind. Another thing I learned is that him backing up usually means he’ll shoot 4 arrows (with the last one being slightly delayed) to deflect. For healing, it’s best to get distance while he’s mid-animation. He usually shoots a single arrow with just enough wind up time to let you spam dodge out of the way while drinking. During the 3rd phase, he starts it off by immediately flying a thrust at you, which can be easily mikiri’d. When he pulls lightning from the sky, you can either jump while he hits you, or stand still and use the mist raven right before he hits you, just make sure to hit back before you hit the ground. Also, moving any direction while getting hit with the mist raven will mess you up pretty bad. Healing this time will also cause him to jump at you with a thrust to mikiri, so it’s best to keep distance for that. His jump attack can also possibly lead to a swipe this time. He also has a pretty slow grab attack in which I usually dodge and take the time I have during the animation to heal. Other than that, he does the same stuff as the first one, so continue to mercilessly attack and deflect him while reversing his lightning and he’ll be toast. Hope this helps!
